ai.summary: Forescout researchers built a tool to test if generally available AI models could find security flaws on a limited budget. They examined both open-source code and compiled software whose source code was unavailable, testing an approach attackers could also use. The team confirmed 99 vulnerabilities across 10 TCP/IP stacks, the software components that allow devices to communicate over networks. general.summary: This weekend, we started seeing requests for /mcp-rest/test/tools/list hitting our honeypots. These requests appear to attempt to exploit CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710. Horizon3.ai published a short write-up about how these vulnerabilities can be chained to achieve remote code execution without authentication [Horizon3]

general.summary: A criminal marketplace advertised on cybercrime forums is selling data stolen from computers infected with infostealer malware, along with AI-written profiles of their owners, Hudson Rock has discovered. Marketplace advertisement (Source: Hudson Rock) Each profile describes who appears to own the machine, where that person works and which of their accounts are worth buying.
